import sys

def main():
    input_data = sys.stdin.read().split('\n')
    state = 0  # 64-bit integer, all flags start OFF
    results = []
    
    for line in input_data:
        line = line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        
        parts = line.split()
        op = parts[0].upper()
        
        if op == 'SET':
            i = int(parts[1])
            state |= (1 << i)
        
        elif op == 'CLEAR':
            i = int(parts[1])
            state &= ~(1 << i)
        
        elif op == 'FLIP':
            i = int(parts[1])
            state ^= (1 << i)
        
        elif op == 'TEST':
            i = int(parts[1])
            result = (state >> i) & 1
            results.append(str(result))
        
        elif op == 'COUNT':
            # Count number of ON flags
            results.append(str(bin(state).count('1')))
        
        elif op == 'ALL':
            # Check if all 64 flags are ON
            all_on = (state == (1 << 64) - 1)
            results.append('1' if all_on else '0')
        
        elif op == 'ANY':
            # Check if any flag is ON
            results.append('1' if state != 0 else '0')
        
        elif op == 'NONE':
            # Check if no flag is ON
            results.append('1' if state == 0 else '0')
        
        elif op == 'PRINT':
            # Print current state as 64-bit binary string
            results.append(format(state, '064b'))
        
        elif op == 'AND':
            # AND with a given mask (provided as integer)
            mask = int(parts[1])
            state &= mask
        
        elif op == 'OR':
            mask = int(parts[1])
            state |= mask
        
        elif op == 'XOR':
            mask = int(parts[1])
            state ^= mask
    
    print('\n'.join(results))

main()
